newsitem.title: USA: CBOT old crop soybeans surge on export rumors.
newsitem.headline: CBOT old crop soybeans surge on export rumors.

text.p: CBOT old crop soybean futures surged in fast dealings on Wednesday, led by August on rumors of export business to Europe and China, pit sources said.
U.S. exporters could not confirm the deals but floor traders noted that U.S. old crop soybeans were priced competitively with South American supplies following recent steep declines.
Old crop stocks remain tight and an uptick in demand would further strain supplies, the traders said.

July continued to draw strength from the lack of deliveries posted against that contract. Rumors had circulated last week that a commercial firm intended to deliver but several commercial firms covered short positions earlier this week, a move traders said lessened the likelihood of deliveries.
In opening trade, Tenco Inc bought one million bushels August, pit sources said.
At 0944 CDT, soybeans were up 12 to two cents per bushel with August up 12 at $7.34.
